hints: Focus on what a C=C needs to show cis-trans isomerism, think about the two groups attached to each carbon of the double bond.
Draw out $\text{Cl}_2\text{C}=\text{CClCH}_3$ and notice that one carbon of the double bond has two identical chlorine atoms on it.
Check the other three structures to see that both carbons of each double bond carry two different groups, so only one structure fails the test.
walkthrough:
**Recall the rule for cis-trans isomerism**

For an alkene to show cis-trans isomerism, each carbon of the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ must have two different groups attached to it.

Rule:
$$\text{each C of C=C must be attached to two different groups}$$

**Draw and test 1,1,2-trichloropropene**

Its structure is $\text{Cl}_2\text{C}=\text{C(Cl)CH}_3$.

Left carbon has $\text{Cl}$ and $\text{Cl}$, which are identical. Right carbon has $\text{Cl}$ and $\text{CH}_3$, which are different. Because one carbon has identical groups, cis-trans is impossible.

**Check the other alkenes all can show it**

$\text{1,2,3-trichloropropene}$ is $\text{ClCH}=\text{C(Cl)CH}_2\text{Cl}$, $\text{1-chlorobut-1-ene}$ is $\text{ClCH}=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, and $\text{1-chlorobut-2-ene}$ is $\text{ClCH}_2\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3$.

In each case both carbons of the double bond have two different groups, so all three can exist as cis and trans forms. Only the first compound cannot.

options.A: Structure is $\text{CCl}_2=\text{CClCH}_3$. C-1 carries two identical Cl atoms, so swapping positions gives the same molecule. The condition for cis-trans isomerism fails, so it does not show cis-trans isomerism.
options.B: Structure is $\text{ClCH}=\text{CClCH}_2\text{Cl}$. C-1 has H and Cl, C-2 has Cl and $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$. Both carbons have two different groups, so cis and trans isomers exist. Students who miscount the substituents may think it cannot.
options.C: Structure is $\text{ClCH}=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. C-1 has H and Cl, C-2 has H and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Both carbons have two different groups, so it shows cis-trans isomerism.
options.D: Structure is $\text{ClCH}_2\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3$. C-2 has H and $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$, C-3 has H and $\text{CH}_3$. Both carbons have two different groups, so it shows cis-trans isomerism. It is a classic example students should recognise.
